narrative: The company raised $500 million in new stock to fund preparations for a potential launch, ahead of the FDA's decision. The trial reached its readout without a financing event beforehand; this raise came after, for the next stage.

checks.a1: Supported. The Phase 3 trial met both co-primary endpoints, NASH resolution and fibrosis improvement, at both doses tested. This does not establish the size of the benefit against the field's history of Phase 3 failures.
checks.a2: Supported. The FDA accepted the application for review, granted Priority Review, and set a target decision date. This is acceptance for review, not the approval decision itself.
checks.a3: Partly supported, narrowly read. The reported raise came in September 2023, after the December 2022 readout, to fund launch preparations rather than to reach it. This does not establish whether cash was sufficient for the years beyond the readout.
checks.a4: Partly supported on timing. The FDA's target decision date, set in September 2023, falls after this five-year window closes. This record does not show whether the price had already reflected the science by then.
checks.a5: Unresolved. The starting record leaves the clinical and regulatory questions open. It does not establish a position either way.

assumptions.text: The Phase 2 biopsy results will replicate in a large Phase 3.
The regulator will agree a trial design that this drug can pass.
Cash is enough to reach the readout without a dilutive raise.
Even if the drug works, five years is too long for the price to reward it.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.
